examples.name: Anime, English dub only
examples.description: Only takes anime releases with an English audio track: marked dubbed, English audio, dual audio, multi audio or JA+EN, or from a group that releases English dubs (Golumpa, KaiDubs, KamiFS, KS, torenter69, Yameii). Subtitles don't count: Dual-Subs, Multi-Sub and Eng-Subs score nothing. A release that names another audio language and not English (PT-BR, Dublado, Latino, Castellano, VF, German DL, ITA-JAP, Hindi, German Dubbed…) scores -1000, even when it says dual audio. The profile needs 100, so subtitle-only releases are skipped. Set each show to series type Anime and this profile. Sonarr only; for films, copy the three custom formats to Radarr with the same scores.

examples.name: x265 first, smallest size
examples.description: Prefers x265 and takes the best x265 it can find at the smallest size; with no x265 it takes anything from SD up, so a show that only exists in SD (old anime) is still grabbed. Every quality from SDTV to 1080p (to 2160p in x265-4k) is in one group, so only the scores rank releases. Tiers: 1080p +2000, 720p +1500, SD 0, x265 +1000. x265 beats one step up in resolution (x265 720p over x264 1080p) but never HD (x264 720p over x265 SD), so an x265 SD release never replaces an HD file. Within a tier: Blu-ray +20, WEB +10, 10-bit +5, and -5 for each size step the file is over (films 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 15, 20 GB; episodes 0.5 to 6 GB; a season pack counts as one big release). Upgrades go on until the top score (x265 Blu-ray 10-bit under the first size step); a smaller file at the same resolution counts as an upgrade. CAM, telesync and remuxes are left out. Every name starts with x265-, so nothing of yours is changed except the quality sizes: those only get low minimums that catch broken releases (they apply to the whole app; keep yours if you like).
